newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees '96 actual foreign investment up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: China sees '96 actual foreign investment up 10 pct.

text.p: Foreign investment has continued to pour into China this year, with officials expecting actual investment to rise by at least 10 percent compared with 1995, the Hong Kong-based China News Agency said.

In the first 11 months, China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation approved 22,034 new contracts by foreign investors, the agency said in a report carried by Hong Kong's Wen Wei Po newspaper on Saturday.
Contracted foreign investment between January and November reached $66.5 billion, while actual investment was $36.9 billion, the report said.
Actual foreign investment for the whole year was expected to exceed $40 billion, rising by 10 percent compared with last year, it added.
That figure placed China first among the world's developing countries in terms of attracting foreign investment and in second place overall, it said.
China's accumulated contracted foreign investment has reached $462.4 billion, the report said without giving dates. Actual foreign investment exceeded $171.8 billion.

In the three years from 1993 to 1995 alone, China attracted $99.2 billion worth of actual foreign investment, or 73.3 percent of the total since paramount leader Deng Xiaoping launched economic reforms and opened China's doors to the outside world in 1978, it said.

In 1995, China's total actual foreign investment reached $37.5 billion, placing China second in the world -- outpaced only by the United States -- in terms of attracting foreign investment for the third successive year, it said.
